skill.name: Verification & Quality Assurance
skill.description: Documents Ruflo verification workflows for truth scoring, CI guards, quality reports, monitoring exports, and rollback procedures.
skill.summary: Use Ruflo verification guidance to check code quality and manage rollback workflows.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Static analysis mostly matched Markdown examples, inline command names, and sample CI snippets rather than executable skill code. No prompt injection or hidden malware intent was found, but rollback guidance can discard local work if an agent runs it without explicit confirmation.

remediation.issue: Rollback examples can discard local changes.
remediation.suggestion: Require git status, backup, dry-run, and explicit user confirmation before rollback or git reset commands.

remediation.issue: Monitoring examples export verification data to external services.
remediation.suggestion: Add consent and redaction guidance before sending reports to Prometheus, DataDog, or custom webhooks.

remediation.issue: The DataDog example places an API key in a query string.
remediation.suggestion: Show header-based authentication and warn that URL query secrets can appear in logs.

remediation.issue: Documentation mixes shipped features with design-only features.
remediation.suggestion: Separate current commands from aspirational workflows so agents do not attempt unavailable automation.

content.user_title: Verify Code Quality with Ruflo Guards
content.value_statement: Code and agent outputs can regress without clear signals. This skill documents Ruflo verification guards, truth scores, reports, and rollback workflows for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Documents Ruflo truth score commands for repository and agent output review.
Explains CI guard layers for smoke tests, tool audits, witness manifests, and history tracking.
Shows verification report formats for JSON, HTML, CSV, and Markdown summaries.
Provides rollback commands for last-good, commit-based, selective, and dry-run workflows.
Includes GitHub Actions and GitLab CI examples for verification gates.
Describes monitoring exports for Prometheus, DataDog, and custom webhooks.
limitations: Some truth scoring, dashboard, and auto-rollback features are described as partly aspirational.
The package contains documentation only, not an implementation of the Ruflo verifier.
Ruflo alpha, Node.js, Git, and repository-specific files are required for many workflows.
Rollback and reset commands can remove work if used without review.

use_cases.title: Validate Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Run documented verification checks before publishing a package or merging a high-risk change.

use_cases.title: Add CI Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Use the CI examples to require verification results before pull requests are accepted.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Output
use_cases.description: Apply truth score and report workflows to evaluate generated code before it reaches users.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Basic Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to choose a basic Ruflo verification check for my repository. Include what the result means and when rollback is unsafe.

prompt_templates.title: Plan CI Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a CI verification gate for my project. Summarize required checks, reports, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Rollback Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review a failed verification result. Recommend a rollback path only after listing backup and confirmation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Verification Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to audit our verification coverage across smoke tests, witness manifests, tool descriptions, reports, and monitoring exports.

output_examples.input: A release engineer asks whether a package is ready to publish.
output: Recommended checks include local verification, CI smoke tests, witness verification, and report review.
Rollback is not recommended until the working tree is backed up and the failed files are identified.

output_examples.input: A DevOps engineer wants verification in pull request workflows.
output: The response outlines a quality gate with dependency install, verification run, score review, and artifact upload.
It also notes that external monitoring exports need approval and secret redaction.

output_examples.input: An AI lead wants to evaluate generated code from several agents.
output: The response compares truth score trends, failed criteria, rollback frequency, and report formats.
It separates shipped Ruflo guards from design-only dashboard features.

best_practices: Run verification before merge, release, or automated rollback decisions.
Review generated reports before sending them to external monitoring systems.
Use dry-run and backup steps before any rollback command.
anti_patterns: Do not treat aspirational dashboard features as installed functionality.
Do not run rollback or reset commands without explicit user approval.
Do not place API keys in URLs or shared verification reports.

faq.question: Does this skill implement Ruflo verification itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents Ruflo verification workflows, commands, reports, and CI guard patterns.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What is the main safety concern?
faq.answer: Rollback guidance can discard local changes if commands run without backup and confirmation.

faq.question: Are the monitoring URLs automatic network calls?
faq.answer: No. They are documentation examples for explicit user-configured exports.

faq.question: What should users verify before using it?
faq.answer: Users should confirm Ruflo alpha availability, repository state, Node.js version, and CI file paths.

faq.question: How should teams use the truth score threshold?
faq.answer: Teams should set stricter thresholds for production code and lower thresholds for experiments.
